task_1.title: Strip Proxy-Authorization on cross-host redirects
task_1.description: The default redirect safety policy now treats Proxy-Authorization like other sensitive request headers, removing it when a request is redirected to a different host. Users can still customize the redirect header removal policy through Retry.remove_headers_on_redirect.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that proxy credentials are not forwarded by default when urllib3 follows a redirect to a different host.

expectation.grounded: Retry.DEFAULT_REMOVE_HEADERS_ON_REDIRECT must include Proxy-Authorization in addition to Cookie and Authorization, so the default Retry behavior removes Proxy-Authorization from requests redirected to a different host. Retry.remove_headers_on_redirect remains the public way to supply a different set of headers to remove.
expectation.conceptual: When following redirects across hosts, the library should protect proxy authentication credentials by excluding them from the redirected request unless the caller explicitly configures a different header removal policy.

constraints.grounded: The existing default removal of Cookie and Authorization on cross-host redirects must be preserved. Custom values supplied through Retry.remove_headers_on_redirect must continue to determine which headers are removed instead of forcing the default list.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must improve default credential safety without removing caller control over redirect header handling or weakening existing protections for other sensitive headers.

behavior: The default Retry header removal set now includes Proxy-Authorization.
Requests redirected to a different host with default retry settings will have Proxy-Authorization stripped along with the previously stripped sensitive headers.
Callers that provide Retry.remove_headers_on_redirect can still replace the default removal set with their chosen headers.
acceptance_criteria: When a request containing Proxy-Authorization is redirected to a different host using default retry settings, the redirected request should not include Proxy-Authorization.

When a request containing Cookie, Authorization, and Proxy-Authorization is redirected to a different host using default retry settings, all three sensitive headers should be omitted from the redirected request.

When Retry.remove_headers_on_redirect is explicitly configured, the headers removed on a cross-host redirect should follow that configured set rather than always applying the default sensitive-header set.

When users inspect the default redirect removal policy via Retry.DEFAULT_REMOVE_HEADERS_ON_REDIRECT or a default Retry instance, Proxy-Authorization should be part of the default sensitive-header policy.

task_3.title: Preserve subclass return types for copy-like APIs
task_3.description: The update corrects public type annotations for APIs whose runtime behavior already returns an instance of the concrete class. Retry copying methods and HTTPHeaderDict copy and merge operations should be typed so subclass users retain their subclass type instead of being narrowed to the base class.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that copy-like and state-advancing APIs that preserve the concrete object type at runtime also expose that same concrete type to static type checkers.

expectation.grounded: The return types for urllib3.Retry.new and urllib3.Retry.increment must represent the current concrete Retry subtype rather than always urllib3.Retry. The return types for urllib3.HTTPHeaderDict.copy, urllib3.HTTPHeaderDict.__or__, and urllib3.HTTPHeaderDict.__ror__ must likewise represent the current concrete HTTPHeaderDict subtype. This should allow subclass implementations and callers to use Self-style return contracts without incompatible return-type diagnostics.
expectation.conceptual: When users subclass retry or header dictionary objects, copying, incrementing, or merging them should preserve the subclass type in static typing just as the operations already do at runtime.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the runtime behavior, public signatures beyond return typing, retry counter semantics, header copying semantics, header merge behavior, accepted operands, raised exceptions, or mutation behavior of Retry and HTTPHeaderDict operations.
constraints.conceptual: This is a typing correctness update only; existing working code should continue to behave the same while type checkers become more precise for subclasses.

behavior: Static type checkers infer that Retry.new returns the same concrete Retry subtype as the receiver.
Static type checkers infer that Retry.increment returns the same concrete Retry subtype as the receiver.
Static type checkers infer that HTTPHeaderDict.copy returns the same concrete HTTPHeaderDict subtype as the receiver.
Static type checkers infer that HTTPHeaderDict merge operations using the union operator return the same concrete HTTPHeaderDict subtype as the participating HTTPHeaderDict receiver.
Runtime object creation, retry state updates, header storage, header extension, merge ordering, and error behavior remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given a subclass of Retry, when a caller invokes new on an instance of that subclass, the statically inferred return type should be that subclass.

Given a subclass of Retry, when a caller invokes increment on an instance of that subclass or delegates to the base implementation from an override with a Self-style return, the statically inferred return type should be compatible with that subclass.
Given a subclass of HTTPHeaderDict, when a caller invokes copy on an instance of that subclass, the statically inferred return type should be that subclass.

Given a subclass of HTTPHeaderDict, when a caller merges headers with the union operator and the subclass instance is the HTTPHeaderDict operand, the statically inferred result type should be that subclass.
When existing Retry and HTTPHeaderDict operations are executed, their observable runtime behavior should match the previous release aside from improved type information.

task_2.title: Treat Negative Read Amounts as Unlimited
task_2.description: urllib3 2.2.2 fixes response body reads so negative integer read amounts are accepted as an unlimited read, matching the behavior of omitted or None sizes, instead of causing unexpected failures or partial-read handling.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 response read operations accept negative integer amt values as an unlimited read, equivalent to omitting amt or passing None.

expectation.grounded: For urllib3.response.HTTPResponse, read(amt), read1(amt), and read_chunked(amt) should treat any negative integer amt the same as None: read and read1 return the remaining available response bytes according to their normal unlimited-read behavior, and read_chunked yields chunks until the response is exhausted. The same negative-amt semantics should apply to the urllib3.contrib.emscripten response wrapper. Non-negative amt values must keep their existing bounded-read behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users can pass -1 or another negative read size to consume the remaining response body, consistent with common file-like object behavior, without receiving an unexpected exception.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing behavior for omitted amt, amt=None, amt=0, or positive amt values. Preserve decode_content handling, chunk ordering, end-of-response behavior, and the distinction between full-response reads and bounded partial reads for non-negative sizes.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only expand accepted read-size inputs; existing response streaming, decoding, chunking, and partial-read semantics should remain compatible.

behavior: HTTPResponse.read with a negative amt behaves like an unlimited read and returns all remaining bytes instead of treating the negative value as a bounded buffer request.
HTTPResponse.read1 with a negative amt behaves like its no-limit form and returns available response bytes without failing because the size is negative.
HTTPResponse.read_chunked with a negative amt yields response chunks until exhaustion, matching the behavior of no amt or amt=None.
The Emscripten response wrapper treats negative amt values as unlimited reads rather than as partial reads.
Zero and positive amt values continue to request bounded reads using the existing semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Given a non-preloaded response with remaining body data, when HTTPResponse.read is called with -1 or another negative integer amt, it should return the same remaining bytes as an unlimited read.
Given a response with remaining body data, when HTTPResponse.read1 is called with a negative integer amt, it should use the same observable behavior as read1 with no size limit.
Given a chunked response, when HTTPResponse.read_chunked is called with a negative integer amt, it should yield chunks through the end of the response in the same order as an unlimited chunked read.
When amt is 0 or a positive integer, response read methods should continue to respect the requested size instead of treating it as unlimited.
When the Emscripten response wrapper receives a negative integer amt, it should consume the response as an unlimited read and should not apply partial-read behavior solely because amt is negative.
